paths.description: Homepage and font discovery entry; global preferences, consent, performance, security and network.
Sans-serif theme listing representing category/result lists and preview controls.
Matcha Mint font detail representing metadata, custom preview and primary download action.
Search results for serif, representing the primary query journey.
Account sign-in representing forms, autofill, validation and authentication.
Long-form help content representing documentation and scroll orientation.
French locale representing translated routes and locale formatting.
Missing route representing HTTP failure and recovery.

findings.summary: The first-party interface stays light when the user requests dark mode.
findings.evidence: The dark-media probe matched prefers-color-scheme: dark but computed body background remained rgb(255,255,255), text rgb(0,0,0), and color-scheme was normal. The dark screenshot is visually unchanged.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and retint first-party surfaces with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark(); ensure the consent UI follows the same preference.

findings.summary: Full-page navigation swaps are abrupt and do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found no view-transition CSS, and representative navigation uses classic MPA links with no cross-document transition rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Add @view-transition { navigation: auto } and stable view-transition-name values for the persistent header and content regions, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Long listing and FAQ pages provide no scroll-state-aware orientation aid.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found no scroll-state/container-query support; the 2,178px mobile layout and long FAQ screenshot show static chrome and no progress or compact sticky navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact sticky header or unobtrusive progress/orientation affordance that reacts to scroll state without obscuring content.

findings.summary: A consent interstitial blocks all content on first load.
findings.evidence: Desktop, mobile, dark and FAQ screenshots show a viewport-dimming modal before any interaction; it demands a choice about 272 partners before the font catalog can be used.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the blocking first-load wall with a concise, non-modal consent notice; keep refusal as prominent as acceptance and defer optional processing until a choice.

findings.summary: The blocking consent UI is third-party custom iframe chrome rather than a robust semantic dialog.
findings.evidence: axe found an untitled iframe; the DOM/platform probe found zero dialog, popover or details elements, while screenshots show a modal surface. In one detail capture its iframe content rendered blank while still blocking the page.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a properly named native dialog only if modality is necessary, with Escape/light-dismiss behavior, focus containment and a first-party fallback if the consent provider fails.

findings.summary: Mobile browsers receive a scaled-down 980px desktop layout.
findings.evidence: At a requested 360x800 viewport, layout metrics reported no viewport meta and an effective 980px layout/visual viewport at scale 0.367; the screenshot shows tiny desktop content rather than reflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Add width=device-width, initial-scale=1 and rebuild the fixed 965/980px shell with fluid intrinsic layout and responsive regions.

findings.summary: Reused catalog components are fixed to the page shell rather than adapting to available space.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found no container queries, while French CSS evidence includes legacy 965px padding/margin compensation and floated physical columns.
findings.suggestedFix: Make list cards and navigation self-contained with intrinsic sizing and container queries where their composition changes.

findings.summary: Many controls are too small for touch.
findings.evidence: Login probe measured text fields and buttons at 21px high and the remember checkbox at 13x13px; the scaled mobile page makes them smaller still. Keyboard focus remained visible, but touch sizing is inadequate.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide at least 44x44 CSS-pixel activation areas for primary controls, increase spacing, and preserve native :focus-visible outlines.

findings.summary: The core browse-to-download journey is interrupted before it can start.
findings.evidence: First-load screenshots on home, listing, detail and FAQ archetypes show the 272-partner consent wall covering the primary catalog and download controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Allow browsing and downloading without forcing a tracking decision; load optional ad/analytics code only after freely given consent.

findings.summary: Mobile loading misses the good LCP range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 7.0s, Speed Index 4.0s and time-to-interactive 7.0s, producing a performance score of 0.68; the controlled desktop trace was faster at 1.06s LCP.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise actual catalog content, remove consent/ad work from the critical path, and verify field/mobile LCP after deployment.

findings.summary: Caching and critical delivery are inefficient.
findings.evidence: HAR summary lists many first-party images/CSS without useful cache headers and confirms parser-blocking classic scripts df5.js, key.js, alpha.js and themesv9_en.js without async/defer/module.
findings.suggestedFix: Add long-lived immutable caching for versioned assets and defer or move non-critical classic scripts; keep only essential CSS in the critical path.

findings.summary: Third-party script code dominates a simple catalog page.
findings.evidence: The HAR transferred 845,527 bytes; 771,937 bytes (91%) were third-party, including a 355,942-byte CMP, 257,136 bytes of ad scripts and 154,650 bytes from Tag Manager.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove nonessential vendors, gate optional scripts behind consent and interaction, and budget third-party JavaScript by user value.

findings.summary: Core controls and images lack accessible names and labels.
findings.evidence: axe found 19 missing image alternatives, an unlabeled search input, eight unnamed links and an untitled iframe on home; listing/detail add unnamed selects, and login username/password are unlabeled.
findings.suggestedFix: Add explicit labels and autocomplete, meaningful alt text or empty alt for decoration, discernible link names, named frames, and semantic landmarks.

findings.summary: Small metadata and consent text fail WCAG contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports 3.54:1 for 11px #888 text on white; axe found 3 home consent failures and 9 listing failures.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken secondary text to meet 4.5:1 at its current size and audit every consent state as well as first-party catalog metadata.

findings.summary: Pages lack a logical heading and landmark structure.
findings.evidence: Home has no headings; login only has H3 Login. axe reports no main landmark, dozens of regions outside landmarks, unnamed links and tabindex=1 on search.
findings.suggestedFix: Use header/nav/main/footer landmarks, one descriptive H1 per page, a logical heading hierarchy, and natural DOM tab order without positive tabindex.

findings.summary: The mobile presentation is too small and cramped to read comfortably.
findings.evidence: The 360px screenshot scales a 980px canvas to 0.367, reducing already-small 11px metadata and dense menus to illegible sizes.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a responsive viewport and fluid typography/layout; maintain comfortable line-height, spacing and readable minimum text sizes.

findings.summary: The page does not reflow at a narrow viewport and exposes undersized controls.
findings.evidence: No viewport meta was present; the 360px test stayed 980px wide at page scale 0.367, while login controls measured 13-21px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Add the standard viewport declaration, ensure 320/360px reflow without two-dimensional scrolling, and enlarge activation targets.

findings.summary: The document and image stack use legacy or incomplete asset practices.
findings.evidence: The page declares HTML 4 Transitional and ISO-8859-1/Windows-1252; Lighthouse failed its doctype audit. Images primitive found 19 legacy PNG/GIF images, 2 missing dimensions and 7 below-fold images without lazy loading.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve standards-mode HTML5 as UTF-8, add explicit intrinsic image dimensions, and modernise/lazy-load noncritical imagery where appropriate.

findings.summary: The page is excluded from back/forward cache.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports two BFCache blockers: Cache-Control: no-store on the main resource and on a JavaScript network response.
findings.suggestedFix: Avoid no-store where sensitive data does not require it and audit third-party requests so back/forward navigation can restore instantly.

findings.summary: The public catalog is crawlable but not mobile-friendly.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse and DOM evidence confirm real href links and crawlability, but the page has no viewport meta and renders a 980px desktop canvas at mobile scale.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a responsive viewport and mobile layout while preserving server-rendered anchors and descriptive text.

findings.summary: There is no sitemap for the large public font archive.
findings.evidence: The homepage has a canonical URL and robots permits principal pages, but /sitemap.xml returns a styled 404 despite many catalog detail URLs.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish sitemap index files for canonical font, theme and author URLs and reference them from robots.txt.

findings.summary: Font detail pages expose no structured entity or social preview metadata.
findings.evidence: The login/general probe found zero JSON-LD and Open Graph tags; detail discoverability confirms a public font entity with title/H1/description that could be represented explicitly.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate schema.org CreativeWork/Product-style JSON-LD as appropriate and Open Graph/Twitter metadata matching each visible font detail.

findings.summary: HTTPS is used, but baseline security headers and cookie attributes are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Headers primitive found no CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, clickjacking, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy. redirector-rootdir is not Secure and both observed cookies use SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Roll out a nonce/hash CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy; set least-permissive Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite cookie attributes.

findings.summary: The page loads a large tracking and advertising surface before a positive choice.
findings.evidence: Trackers found seven third-party origins and Google Ads, Tag Manager and Analytics; HAR shows third parties account for 91% of transferred bytes while the modal describes sharing with 272 partners.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce vendors to those essential for the task, prevent optional network calls before consent, and provide a concise first-party privacy explanation.

findings.summary: Authentication is password-only and lacks modern sign-in assistance.
findings.evidence: No permission prompt was detected on load, but login exposes only username/password, with no autocomplete tokens and no visible passkey/WebAuthn option.
findings.suggestedFix: Add correct username/current-password autocomplete immediately, then offer passkeys/WebAuthn with password fallback and recovery.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defenses are absent.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence found no HSTS, clickjacking protection, CSP/frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy and monitor HSTS, CSP including frame-ancestors, nosniff, strict referrer policy and a minimal permissions policy.

findings.summary: Failure of the consent iframe can leave a blank modal blocking the page.
findings.evidence: The detail-page capture shows an empty white consent panel over dimmed content; because the overlay is third-party and modal, its partial failure prevents access to the download flow.
findings.suggestedFix: Fail open for core catalog access: render consent controls first-party or provide a timed, keyboard-accessible fallback that never traps users behind an empty vendor frame.

findings.summary: Localized pages set language correctly but use direction-fragile physical CSS.
findings.evidence: French probe reported lang=fr, but no dir and numerous fixed left/right floats, offsets, padding and text alignment rules, including the 965px shell.
findings.suggestedFix: Set explicit direction where needed and replace physical positioning with logical inline/block properties and modern flow layout.

findings.summary: Consent choices are visually and cognitively asymmetric.
findings.evidence: The blocking dialog foregrounds a red Accept all button while Do not accept is a small underlined text link; it describes sharing extensive data with 272 partners and forces a decision before use.
findings.suggestedFix: Present accept and reject with equal prominence, default to no optional processing, shorten the explanation, and permit continued use without tracking.

findings.summary: Blank login submission gives no actionable error feedback.
findings.evidence: After activating Login with empty fields, the screenshot returned to the same form with no visible field-level or summary error; controls lack required/ARIA validation semantics.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate after interaction, associate clear field errors, focus/announce an error summary, and preserve entered values without blame.

findings.summary: Sign-in fields omit autocomplete metadata.
findings.evidence: Login probe shows empty autocomplete values for username and password, preventing reliable password-manager/autofill assistance.
findings.suggestedFix: Use autocomplete=username and autocomplete=current-password, with correct input types and names.

findings.summary: The account flow depends on password-only authentication.
findings.evidence: The login archetype offers username/password and remember-me but no passkey option or explicit modern reauthentication path.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer phishing-resistant passkeys alongside a well-assisted password fallback and document recovery/cancellation paths.

findings.summary: Image delivery uses legacy formats and misses basic deferral metadata.
findings.evidence: Images primitive found 19/19 images in PNG/GIF, no modern formats, seven below-fold images without lazy loading, two missing dimensions and one missing responsive source.
findings.suggestedFix: Use modern formats where they reduce bytes, preserve raster previews where necessary, add dimensions, and lazy-load below-fold noncritical images.

findings.summary: Optional third-party work dominates a lightweight first-party page.
findings.evidence: Only 73,590 transferred bytes were first-party, versus 771,937 third-party bytes for consent, ads and analytics; these scripts load during the initial view.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer or eliminate optional vendors, batch/minimise analytics, and keep background work behind consent and user intent.

findings.summary: The third-party budget is disproportionate to the font-browsing task.
findings.evidence: Eight third-party requests deliver 91% of page bytes; the three largest vendor scripts are 355,942, 190,639 and 154,650 bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Set an explicit third-party byte/request budget and remove or delay integrations that do not directly support font discovery/download.

taskList.title: Make the catalog genuinely responsive and accessible
Remove or redesign the blocking consent wall
Fix labels, names, landmarks, headings and contrast
Reduce/gate third-party scripts and restore good mobile LCP
Deploy security headers and stricter cookie policy
